A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same weight-generation framework, renamed from EnvAd-Diff to DynaDiff. Their complete main texts and appendices contain readable equations, tables and figures supporting a reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on four PDE systems, ERA5 and a Lotka–Volterra case study, including predictive results, ablations and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 reports original PDE and ERA5 experiments, with additional generalization tests, architectural ablations, sampling analyses and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces expert-response distances, a one-dimensional PCA surrogate and single-frame SVR with a sequence-based prompter combining physical statistics and FFT–GRU features. It trains jointly with diffusion using variable-length observations. Appendix J.6 adds an optional environment-regression auxiliary loss. The weight-graph, functional-loss VAE and latent-diffusion backbone remain.

E1.justification: The four main PDE systems and ERA5 remain. However, v1's Lotka–Volterra simulation and symbolic-regression task disappear. v2 adds a distinct cross-system transfer task: joint training on Cylinder Flow, Lambda-Omega and Navier-Stokes followed by evaluation on held-out Kolmogorov Flow with unseen governing equations (Appendix J.3).

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds CVAE and D2NWG as directly evaluated weight-generation competitors, alongside a Not-Adaptive FNO control. Figure 4 also adds CVAE and D2NWG to the weight-distribution comparison previously limited to generated weights and experts. D2NWG's underlying work was already cited in v1, but was not evaluated there.

E3.justification: Conditioning changes from a single initial frame to a default ten-frame observation sequence. The reported Kolmogorov FNO depth changes from eight layers to four (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 4). New protocols include quadrant-based extrapolation, held-out-system zero/one-trajectory adaptation measured by prediction length above SSIM 0.8, and scaled-baseline and accuracy-matched timing controls. Main simulation ranges and rollout horizons remain.

E4.justification: Beyond retained initialization, functional-loss and model-zoo studies, v2 adds graph-versus-sequence and single-versus-two-stage ablations, observation-length sensitivity, neuron permutations, auxiliary supervision, attention analysis, sampling stability and baseline-scaling controls. It also adds extrapolation and held-out-system analyses. The LV symbolic-regression case disappears, while prompter analysis changes from surrogate-label prediction to decoding physical coefficients.

E5.justification: Both main tables report means and standard deviations from five runs; no increase in that run count is documented. v2 adds Welch's t-tests across the main benchmark settings (Table 5) and a separate 100-sample generation study across ten environments, reporting mean, standard deviation, worst and best RMSE (Table 18). These substantially extend statistical assessment.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises multiple results: proposed-model Cylinder Flow in-domain RMSE changes from 0.053 to 0.063, Kolmogorov out-domain RMSE from 0.084 to 0.079, and DPOT's Kolmogorov out-domain RMSE from 0.091 to 0.084. Numerous comparator, transfer, ablation and cost results are added; LV recovered equations are removed. Changed methods and settings prevent treating these updates as uniform same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v1 contains model and loss equations but no comparable generalization analysis. v2 Section 3.4 and Appendix G introduce oracle prompts, functional Lipschitz and latent-reconstruction assumptions, an error decomposition and a derived empirical generator-error bound (Equations 7–12). This is substantive new mathematical reasoning, although the final bound concerns empirical generator error under assumptions.

C1.justification: The central conditioning problem is redefined around short observation sequences and the new dynamics-informed prompter. The abstract and conclusion replace the headline 1M-versus-500M comparison with a reported 10.78% average improvement over competitive baselines, and elevate amortized deployment efficiency to a central benefit. Full-weight generation without fine-tuning remains the core idea, and the small-predictor comparison remains in the experimental discussion.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations involving architectural attention structure, permutation robustness, transferable dynamics, sampling stability and offline-versus-deployment cost tradeoffs. Appendix J.1 qualifies the Lambda-Omega advantage as statistically unconvincing. The dedicated limitation changes from model-zoo quality and diversity in v1 to fixed generated architectures in v2 Appendix A. The LV-based physical interpretation is removed.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information with VAE/DiT dimensions and depths, per-node encoder/decoder computations, prompter formulas, expert tensor shapes, generator parameter counts, per-expert timing and A100 cost measurements (Appendices D–I, J.8 and K). It also supplies a repository link where v1 promised release after review. These disclosures do not establish changes to every underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning against recent weight-generation research, including LoRA generation, conditional object-detection adaptation and nonstationary weight diffusion. Appendix B and its new Table 2 systematically compare prompting, generated content, representations, generators and supervision across seven competing approaches. This substantially develops the technical novelty argument beyond v1's shorter discussion; publication updates to already cited work are not counted as new research.

P1.justification: Beyond the new title and EnvAd-Diff-to-DynaDiff rename, the abstract, introduction, problem statement, prompter description and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Experimental sections are reorganized, related work and limitations move into appendices, and the supplementary material gains an extensive explanatory structure. This exceeds local language polishing.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. v2 adds paradigm and framework diagrams, attention visualizations, scaling plots and numerous tables; expands the weight-distribution figure with comparator columns; and redraws the weight-aggregation illustration. Several existing displays are retained or relocated, including v1 Figure 7 becoming v2 Figure 13.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evaluation and transparency gaps: v1 lacked direct weight-generation competitors and ablations isolating the graph and two-stage design, while v2 supplies both, broader transfer tests and much fuller implementation and cost information. These substantially strengthen assessment of the central contribution. Changed observation settings limit score comparisons, the LV case study is lost, and the new theory remains conditional. Appendix J.1 also misnames the Kolmogorov comparator as GEPS although Table 1 identifies DPOT. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in experimental scrutiny and reproducibility.
